# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe requires the actual trained `NextItNetModel` at `view.model`. It accesses item embeddings and residual `NextItNetBlock` outputs through the host adapter. `view.log2feats(sequence)` supplies finite FP32 `B × L × H` features; the user representation is gathered at the **maximum nonzero sequence index**, correctly handling left padding. `view.predict_score` scores candidates. Backbone implementation details are not supplied here.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` reads training histories, category routing and batches `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`. It uniquely matches encoded histories and aligned targets to training endpoints, rejecting ambiguous matches. It selects at most 32 users, one event each, from ten batches. Each event receives its target plus up to 99 unique unseen alternatives, shared across conditions.

Diagnosis temporarily enables evaluation mode and deterministic FP32 execution, then restores modes, backend settings and RNG states.

# Probes & Metrics

- Outcomes are `[target-minus-best-alternative margin, target rank, diagnostic HR@10]`. Higher margins/hits and lower ranks indicate better target ranking.
- Summaries average draws within users, then weight users equally, reporting all/repeat/novel strata. Paired user-bootstrap intervals require at least ten users.
- Coverage, execution errors and numerical controls distinguish measured effects from unavailable work.
- Separate callable helpers estimate embedding cosine similarity and training positive–negative margins, but **`run_full_diagnosis` does not invoke them**.

# Perturbation & Tests

Stage 1 compares clean inputs with three earlier-item permutations and three endpoint replacements. Stage 2 runs only when candidate scores change beyond numerical tolerance. At two intermediate residual sites, hooks replace only the readout-position activation: clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption, each compared with its own recipient baseline.

Other-user donors match original history length and endpoint ID. Their results are descriptive because donors may be reused. Controls check readout agreement, batch consistency, bounded future invariance, repeatability, activation layout/padding, and no-op/identity patches. Failed sites invalidate their patch results.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The return contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, including status, summaries, paired condition comparisons, donor summaries, controls, coverage, errors and replay-manifest location. The interpreter prompt requests a grounded JSON interpretation.

Measurements concern conditional training sensitivity, not host validation or generalization. Hybrid activation patches do not establish universal causality. Export parity, complete dependency paths, other temporal positions and unavailable metadata remain unverified. A 120-second category cap can leave partial results.
